newsitem.title: DUBAI: Syria says no movement on peace track with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Syria says no movement on peace track with Israel.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam has brushed aside Israeli suggestions their bilateral Middle East peace talks are about to resume after a 10-month break.

"There is no movement until now regarding resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he said after talks with United Arab (UAE) President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan in Abu Dhabi late on Tuesday.
"The Israeli media campaign expressing optimism regarding restaring talks aims at misleading public opinion," Khaddam added in remarks carried by the UAE official WAM news agency.

Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara arrived in Abu Dhabi earlier on Tuesday as part of a regional tour to drum up support for Syria's peace stand after Israel and the PLO settled their deadlock on the West Bank town of Hebron earlier this month, Gulf Arab newspapers have said.
Syria, they said, did not want Arab countries to pressure it to restart talks with Israel because of the recent deal.
Both Syrian officials have been to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
"He (Khaddam) denied that any pressure was being exerted on Syria to jump start the talks and said Syria would not bow to any pressure when the matter dealt with its land and pride," WAM said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that the United States was trying to find a "bridging formula" to get both states to revive their talks.
Netanyahu and other Israeli officials have said there were contacts with Syria through the United States, the main sponsor of the five-year-old process and other channels.
"Syria remains committed to the peace process and to the resumption of talks from where they ended including Israel's acceptance of committments made by the previous government," Khaddam said.
Netanyahu unseated former prime minister Shimon Peres in elections last May and has since challenged the principle of land-for-peace, the basis of the current peace process.
Syria demands the return of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Israel broke off talks with Syria after a series of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel last February and March.
